evidence.observation: "Milestone closure replays two source documents, a duplicate observation, one accepted group, one declined group and an interrupted restart. Compare the final model digest, surviving references, located evidence, decision identities, counters and terminal reason between uninterrupted and resumed runs."

The duplicate-observation growth is "The integrated test in tests/test_consolidation_loop.py", and the comparison is a separate "recovery comparison runs the same leave and merge in separate temporary workspaces". In the test file, test_recovery_matches_uninterrupted_history uses the workspace() fixture: two directly written facts with distinct codes 2 and 3, with no additive preview/apply and no duplicate tuple. test_located_additive_growth_then_consolidation has no interruption and no uninterrupted/resumed comparison. Its decline happens only inside `while set(info["group"]["members"]) != desired`, so it may leave zero groups.

concerns.recommendation: Add one replay test that does all of the following in one run: additive growth from a second document with a duplicate observation, a guaranteed leave, an accepted merge, and an interrupted restart. Compare the uninterrupted and resumed runs field by field. Alternatively, have the close ruling explicitly accept the split and explain why it is equivalent.
concerns.title: Amendment 5 closure replay is split into separate tests, and no single run contains all five required elements

evidence.observation: "Put the replay and exact results in the milestone close record."

The section only describes what the tests compare ("It compares the complete model bytes, all durable decision fields (including IDs and work counters), and the resulting report and terminal reason"). It records no final model digest, decision IDs, counter values, terminal reason string, pytest summary or test node IDs.

concerns.recommendation: Record the exact observed values from the replay: model sha256, decision IDs, items/pairs counters, the terminal reason (for example no-eligible-group) and the verbatim pytest summary for the named tests, each tied to the code commit that produced it.
concerns.title: The close record describes the replay but gives none of its exact results

evidence.observation: "The post-repair focused and RF6 checks returned 32 passed in 17.73s before the directory-alias regression was added. The phase structure, CLI, packaging, install, doctor, disclosure and CG1–3 selection on the earlier implementation returned 1053 passed... The wheel test preceded the final review repairs."

"Shared sample population evaluation now serves both additive admission and the reviewed mutation check." This changes the CG1 admission path, but the only check reported on the final bytes is "16 passed" for tests/test_consolidation_loop.py. The front-matter gate also lists `pytest -q tests/test_consolidation_loop.py tests/test_rf6_query_policy.py` with exit 0, while the prose says that run predates the final test.

concerns.recommendation: Re-run the CG1–3 selection, the packaging/install checks and the offline-wheel terminal example on the final commit. Record the verbatim summaries, and make the gate front matter match the prose.
concerns.title: Broad, CG1 and packaged-wheel checks were not re-run on the final code after the shared admission refactor

evidence.observation: "recompute candidates after apply and stop at the configured threshold" and "Terminate when no eligible unresolved group meets the selected minimum score". src/gnd/evolve/consolidation.py filters on `g["score"] >= minimum_score` (default 0), but every step() call in tests/test_consolidation_loop.py uses the default. The only no-eligible-group result comes after all groups are resolved.

concerns.recommendation: Add a test that sets minimum_score just above and exactly at an eligible group's score. Assert no-eligible-group on one side and needs-decision on the other, and report the result in the close record.
concerns.title: The configured minimum-score stop is never tested on either side of the threshold

evidence.observation: "The replay simulates process interruption at publication and finalization boundaries." In the tests, the pre-finalize case (test_stale_unstaged_intent_can_be_superseded) replaces EvolutionService.apply entirely ("before staging"). It then appends to the model and asserts "superseded-before-publication", so nothing interrupted at publication is recovered to completion.
"It injects an interruption at finalization after the model CAS." Only the finalization interruption gets an equivalence comparison.

concerns.recommendation: Either narrow the claim to "before staging (supersession) and after CAS at finalization", or add an interruption between evidence staging and the model CAS whose recovery is compared with an uninterrupted run.
concerns.title: The publication-boundary interruption claim is broader than the tested before-staging case

evidence.observation: "Bound the loop by maximum decisions and discovery work." The only loop-bound tests are `step(path, max_items=0)` and `step(path, max_decisions=0)`. In consolidation.py, `spent` sums work only from state["completed"], so discovery work in read-only needs-decision calls is never charged, and max_pairs exhaustion is not tested at the loop level.

concerns.recommendation: Test the decision and items/pairs limits at exact and one-less values after at least one completed decision. Also state in the record whether probing steps count against discovery work.
concerns.title: Loop decision and discovery-work limits are tested only at zero, and probe work is not charged

evidence.observation: "Changing the supporting source of a declined group offers it again." test_changed_evidence_reopens_a_declined_group copies the other fact's existing span into fact 0's provenance.spans and rewrites model.orm.json directly. No new source document is supplied and no additive apply is used.

concerns.recommendation: Either describe the test as an evidence-span change, or reopen through a public additive apply that cites a new document.
concerns.title: The reopen-after-changed-evidence claim edits the model directly rather than changing a source through the public path

evidence.observation: "use the issue reproduction and the criterion in §4 as an acceptance pair" and "Milestone closure requires a replay across phases, a disposition for each issue and an inventory of unverified claims."

"The reporter's two large models were unavailable... No paid grower effectiveness trial was selected." The record does not say whether these were optional corpus trials or mandatory criteria. It also does not say whether the #338/#339 reproduction examples were run as acceptance pairs.

concerns.recommendation: Add a short table that marks each criterion mandatory or optional, links it to its evidence, and lists the unverified claims, including the reporter corpus counts.
concerns.title: The close record does not separate mandatory criteria from optional corpus trials or list the issue reproductions

summary: The CG3 workflow covers the four decisions, binds each decision to its digests and recovers after finalization, and the tests mostly match the descriptions. The milestone close does not yet meet Amendment 5. The required replay is split across tests that each lack part of what it must contain. The close record gives no exact replay results. The broad, packaging and CG1-adjacent checks ran on code older than the final bytes, even though the change refactored shared CG1 admission. The configured minimum-score stop is never tested.
